title: Personal Credit Cards: when the annual fee is billed and when it is refunded at closing
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: annual fee billing and refund at closing

This policy covers the annual fee of the Personal Credit Cards line: which statement carries it, the first-year waiver, the military exclusion, the once-a-year limit and the refund when the cardholder closes the card soon after the fee posted. The fee amount and whether the first-year waiver applies are the tier's own terms.

## Policy clauses

1. The tier's annual fee is billed as an annual fee on the statement that closes in the account's anniversary month each year; the anniversary month is the month of the account's opening date.
2. When the tier's first-year waiver applies, no annual fee is billed on the first anniversary-month statement after opening that falls within twelve months of the opening date.
3. No annual fee is billed while the military rate cap is active on the account.
4. A tier whose annual fee is 0.00 posts no annual fee entry.
5. At most one annual fee is billed per account year.
6. When the cardholder closes the account within 30 calendar days after the annual fee posted, the fee is reversed in full on the bank error ground. After that window the fee is never refunded or prorated.

## Worked illustrations (hypothetical accounts on a tier with the first-year waiver)

- Opened 12 April, statement closing on the 20th of each month. The statement closing 20 April of the opening year is after opening, in the anniversary month and within twelve months of opening: no annual fee on it. The statement closing 20 April of the next year is more than twelve months after opening: the annual fee is billed.
- Opened 12 April, statement closing on the 5th. The 5 April statement of the opening year closes before opening. The first anniversary-month statement after opening is 5 April of the next year, which is within twelve months of 12 April: no annual fee on it. The fee is billed on the 5 April statement of the year after that.

## Refund at closing (hypothetical dates)

| Annual fee posted | Account closed | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 5 March | 20 March | within 30 calendar days: reversed in full on the bank error ground |
| 5 March | 20 May | after the window: not refunded and not prorated |

## Basis Q&A

**Q: Is part of the annual fee returned when a card is closed months after the fee posted?**
A: No. After the 30-day window the fee is never refunded or prorated.

**Q: Is an annual fee billed while the customer's military rate cap is active?**
A: No annual fee is billed while the cap is active on the account.
